review: 1:1 שָׁלְמָה נַפְשִׁי — 'my soul is whole/at peace', for طِبْتُ نَفْسًا; the Arabic طاب نفسا is 'my soul was well pleased', and שָׁלֵם is the biblical verb for being whole, which carries the sense without the idiomatic طاب.
2:2 יָם חֶסֶד שׁוֹפֵעַ — 'a brimming sea of grace', for بَحْرُ لُطْفٍ زَاخِر; the Arabic keeps both the sea and the overflowing, and Hebrew keeps both nouns.
4:1–4:2 זֹהַר כְּבוֹד אֵל / וְצֶלֶם הָעֶלְיוֹן — Hebrews 1:3 (זֹהַר כְּבוֹדוֹ וְצֶלֶם עַצְמוּתוֹ); the Arabic بَهَاءَ مَجْدِ اللهِ / وَصُورَةَ الْعَلِيّ is that verse, and Hebrew keeps its two nouns.
5:1 פָּנֶיךָ יֵלְכוּ לְפָנַי — Exodus 33:14 (פָּנַי יֵלֵכוּ); the Arabic سِرْ بِوَجْهِكَ أَمَامِي is 'walk before me with Your face', and the Hebrew keeps the face as the subject that leads.

5:3–5:4 וְיָסוּר הַלַּיְלָה … תּוֹפִיעַ בְּשִׂמְחָה — the Arabic فَيُوَلِّي اللَّيْلُ حِينَ / تَبْدُو بَاسِمًا makes the night flee at Your smiling appearance; Hebrew keeps the same causal order, with the smile rendered as appearing 'in joy'.
